title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic network verifier (plus up to one automated repair iteration) into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. In a preregistered paired design (N=500 tasks stratified into VLAN-change, ACL-change, static-route-change clusters) we used shared_initial_candidate semantics so the same LLM proposal served both arms: (1) baseline — LLM proposal only, and (2) guarded — identical proposal validated and repaired if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs=500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.0); contingency n11=499, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Absolute paired success-rate difference = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B=10,000, seed=1729). The archived exact McNemar two-sided implementation (exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs) produced p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; the measured marginal pass-rate gain from a single repair iteration is therefore small, although the verifier corrected a single concrete baseline failure (artifact-backed). All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic reinspection.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being applied to NetOps tasks including intent→configuration translation, change planning, and automated repair. Operational safety in these systems is widely argued to depend on surrounding engineering—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback—rather than the model alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A common operational architecture is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM proposes a candidate; a deterministic verifier checks machine-formal properties; repairs are applied for violations. Despite conceptual consensus, controlled measurements that isolate the marginal contribution of a verifier while holding the LLM output fixed are scarce. Practitioners therefore lack quantitative guidance on whether modest verifier+repair budgets materially reduce verifier-detected safety violations when baseline proposal quality is already high. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment to answer this narrow operational question under deterministic semantics: given identical initial proposals, how much does integrating a deterministic verifier plus one automated repair iteration reduce verifier-detected safety violations compared to the same LLM proposal without verifier feedback?
sections.related_work: Deterministic and formal verification methods for network configuration (header-space analysis, Batfish-style analyzers, route-model verification) provide machine-checkable properties such as reachability/isolation and update atomicity; these methods underpin practical NetOps verification pipelines [Beckett et al., 2017]. Concurrently, recent NetOps/AIOps system papers and intent-translation research show LLMs applied to intent parsing and configuration generation while emphasizing operational guardrails (e.g., INTA, Confucius, and other agentic NetOps frameworks) [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair patterns and verifier-in-the-loop proposals appear across structured-generation domains and have been instantiated in various workflows [PoeTone; INTA]. Separate work documents LLM failure modes (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and recommends verification or human oversight as mitigations [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. What is missing in the supplied literature is a preregistered ablation that keeps the LLM’s proposal identical across arms and quantifies the marginal verifier+repair effect on a deterministic pass/fail metric; this study provides such an artifact-backed measurement and places it beside those prior works.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026 and froze the research question, inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic task seeds, estimands, analysis executor, retry policy, and stopping rule prior to observing outcomes. Primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM plus deterministic verifier and a single automated repair iteration will yield a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM proposal alone (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, with success defined as zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations according to the verifier’s mapping (validator-spec archived). The preregistration and artifacts are archived (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest).

Task corpus and strata. We generated a deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds. Tasks were stratified into VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters with preregistered allocation 167/167/166; the realized confirmatory set matched that allocation (N=500) and the complete task manifest is archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl for deterministic confirmation. The generator constrained tasks to features the verifier modeled (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}); tasks referencing unmodeled features would have been excluded per preregistration but no confirmatory exclusions occurred in this run (see analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Generation semantics, models, and verifier. To isolate verifier+repair effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate": for each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal that served as the baseline output and was also validated by the guarded arm. The guarded arm invoked up to one automated repair call only when the deterministic verifier reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on that shared candidate. Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini called through the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses); model_configuration.json and execution manifest record the runtime parameters and model_call accounting. The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator specification and the mapping of violation codes to severity are archived in the evidence bundle). The guarded arm permitted a single automated repair iteration per preregistered contract.

Analysis plan and implementations. The preregistered confirmatory test was an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements the two-sided exact McNemar by forming n = n10 + n01 (discordant pairs) and computing an exact binomial two-sided p-value for observed n10 under X∼Binomial(n,0.5) (executor convention documented in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals for the absolute difference used B = 10,000 resamples with bootstrap_seed = 1729; resampling preserves pairing. Missingness treatment, retry policy, and the stopping rule are described in the preregistration and in the execution manifest; execution accounting is recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The run completed with complete_pair_count = 500 and model_calls_used = 501 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls observed = 1). Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002.

Inferential results and uncertainty. The archived exact McNemar two-sided implementation produced p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1) under the executor’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records implementation details). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729) and is recorded in analysis artifacts.

Repair activity and discordant episode provenance. Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1; that single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1): the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verifier pass. The run-level manifests (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirm exactly one repair-stage call and exactly one discordant pair. The full per-task validator_trace, repair_provider_trace (when present), normalized configurations, and provider-call traces for every episode — including the discordant episode — are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/provider_calls/*, and execution/scoring/*. To deterministically locate the corrected episode: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for entries where baseline scoring reports a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass==0) and guarded scoring reports pass==1; because only one such episode exists, that filter returns the single corrected pair and its provider-call and validator traces. The archived validator_trace for that episode records the verifier-reported violation code(s) and the repair-stage response; those archived fields are the basis for the claim that the verifier repaired a concrete baseline failure. We intentionally do not reproduce raw configuration lines or command text here; all low-level traces and the validator’s violation-code→severity mapping are available in the evidence bundle for auditors.

Power and ceiling effects. The preregistration assumed baseline error prevalence near 0.30 for power calculations (N≈384 for 80% power to detect a 10pp absolute reduction). Observed baseline failure prevalence was far lower (1/500), producing a ceiling effect and limiting sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements. As a result, secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts; the analysis artifacts and missingness_summary.csv document these diagnostics.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained experimental regime—single requested model (gpt-5-mini), shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration—the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals and the marginal measured pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This is a conditional result: when baseline proposal quality on verifier-scoped properties is very high, modest verifier+repair budgets may yield negligible pass-rate gains on a composite verifier-scoped metric. Nonetheless, the verifier demonstrated concrete utility by correcting one baseline failure (artifact-backed) and thereby avoided an individual misconfiguration that would otherwise have passed to execution.

Design-choice implications. The shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate the verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals; this scenario matches deployments that must preserve a single human-reviewed proposal and apply repairs rather than regenerate proposals repeatedly. Alternative operational choices—verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repair iterations, different cost models for model calls—could yield larger effect sizes and should be measured under their own preregistrations.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is supported by preregistration, deterministic seeds, and automated exclusion/replacement rules; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity is limited by the verifier’s modeled property set: pass == no preregistered high/medium-severity violations is relative to the verifier’s coverage and severity mapping archived with the validator. If production-critical properties lie outside that scope, the present measurement underestimates the verifier’s practical value. External validity is limited by single-model testing, synthetic tasks, and constrained feature scope; results are not evidence of multi-model or cross-vendor generality.

Statistical nuance. The archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the executor’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs computation and the empirical discordant counts (n=1). With extremely small discordant counts the exact two-sided p-value can be uninformative; the paired-bootstrap CI offers complementary uncertainty quantification. Together these artifacts show that while a point-estimate improvement exists (0.002), inference is constrained by a ceiling effect and by the very small number of discordant outcomes.

Practical recommendations. (1) Measure baseline verifier-scoped error prevalence on representative workloads before allocating costly repair/regeneration budgets: when baseline error is extremely low, marginal pass-rate gains per unit cost may be small. (2) Align verifier coverage to operator-critical properties and expand modeled features where needed; the validator-spec in the evidence bundle enumerates modeled properties and severity mapping. (3) Choose generation semantics consistent with operational priorities: shared-initial_candidate semantics preserve the original proposal for human review and minimize model calls; verifier-guided regeneration may increase final-pass probability at additional model-call cost.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N=500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial convention). This conditional measurement illustrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is very high for verifier-modeled properties and verifier coverage is limited, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a modest verifier+repair budget can be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, though the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures. We recommend practitioners measure baseline error prevalence, align verifier coverage with operator-critical properties, and select generation/repair semantics that match deployment priorities. All preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic reinspection.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces.
